en: be willing to do even at the cost of; not shrink from

examples.ko: 그는 위험을 불사하고 물에 빠진 아이를 구했어요.
examples.en: He saved the child who had fallen into the water, risking danger.

examples.ko: 이 회사는 손해를 불사하며 새로운 사업을 시작했어요.
examples.en: This company started a new business, willing to take a loss.

examples.ko: 선수들은 부상을 불사한 채 끝까지 달렸어요.
examples.en: The players ran to the end, ignoring their injuries.

examples.ko: 부모님은 친척들의 반대를 불사하고 제 선택을 응원해 주셨어요.
examples.en: My parents backed my choice even in the face of our relatives' opposition.

examples.ko: 친구를 돕기 위해서라면 어떤 고생도 불사할 거예요.
examples.en: If it's to help my friend, I'll put up with any hardship.

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 이번 발표를 위해 밤샘도 불사해요.
examples.en: Our team will even pull all-nighters for this presentation.

explain: '위험을 불사하다', '희생을 불사하다'처럼 나쁜 결과나 힘든 일이 있어도 하겠다는 각오를 말할 때 써요. 주로 뉴스, 연설, 글에서 쓰고 일상 대화에서는 '각오하고 하다'처럼 말하는 경우가 많아요. 보통 '-을/를 불사하고' 꼴로 나와요.
explain_en: Used for being ready to accept risk or sacrifice, as in '위험을 불사하다' (do it despite the danger). It appears mostly in news, speeches and writing, while everyday talk uses things like '각오하고 하다' (do it prepared for the worst). It often comes in the form '-을/를 불사하고'.

examples.ko: 대출 상환 날짜가 다음 주 금요일이에요.
examples.en: The loan repayment date is next Friday.
I asked the bank how to repay the loan.

examples.ko: 빚의 상환이 늦어지면 이자가 더 붙어요.
examples.en: If the repayment of a debt is delayed, more interest is added.

examples.ko: 이 상품은 상환 기간이 길어서 부담이 적어요.
examples.en: This product has a long repayment period, so the burden is light.

examples.ko: 그는 학자금 대출 상환을 모두 끝냈어요.
examples.en: He finished all of his student loan repayments.

examples.ko: 상환 능력이 없으면 대출을 받기 어려워요.
examples.en: Without the ability to repay, it is hard to get a loan.

explain: '대출 상환', '원금 상환'처럼 빌린 돈을 갚는 일을 말할 때 써요. 친구에게 빌린 돈은 '갚다'라고 하고, '상환'은 은행, 대출, 채권 같은 금융 이야기에서 써요. '상환하다', '상환되다'와 같이 알아 두세요.
explain_en: Used for paying back borrowed money, as in '대출 상환' (loan repayment) or '원금 상환' (principal repayment). Money borrowed from a friend is '갚다'; '상환' belongs to finance talk about banks, loans and bonds. Learn it together with '상환하다' and '상환되다'.

examples.ko: 대출금은 다음 달에 모두 상환될 거예요.
examples.en: The loan will be fully repaid next month.

examples.ko: 빌린 돈이 제때 상환되지 않아서 문제가 생겼어요.
examples.en: A problem came up because the borrowed money was not repaid on time.
When the principal is repaid, the interest also goes down.
Government bonds are repaid automatically when they mature.

examples.ko: 이 대출은 매달 조금씩 상환되고 있어요.
examples.en: This loan is being paid off a little each month.

examples.ko: 모든 빚이 상환된 날 가족이 함께 식사했어요.
examples.en: On the day all the debt was paid off, the family had a meal together.

explain: '상환하다'는 갚는 사람이 주어이고, '상환되다'는 빚이나 대출금이 주어일 때 써요. '대출금이 상환되다'처럼 돈이 갚아지는 결과를 말하고, 주로 금융 뉴스나 계약서에서 나와요.
explain_en: '상환하다' has the person who pays as its subject, while '상환되다' takes the debt or loan as its subject, as in '대출금이 상환되다'. It describes the result of money being paid back and appears mainly in financial news and contracts.

examples.en: I am paying back my loan a little each month.
It takes five years to repay all of the tuition loan.

examples.ko: 회사는 빌린 돈을 약속한 날짜에 상환했어요.
examples.en: The company repaid the borrowed money on the promised date.
Can you pay off the debt all at once?

examples.ko: 이자와 원금을 나누어 상환하는 방법도 있어요.
examples.en: There is also a way to repay the interest and principal in parts.

examples.ko: 먼저 카드 대금을 상환해야 새 카드를 받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: You have to settle your card balance first to get a new card.

explain: 친구에게 빌린 돈은 '갚다', 은행 대출이나 채무는 '상환하다'를 써요. 보통 '대출금을 상환하다', '빚을 상환하다'처럼 목적어가 돈이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '갚다'가 훨씬 자연스러워요.
explain_en: For money borrowed from a friend, Koreans say '갚다'; for bank loans and debts they use '상환하다'. The object is usually money, as in '대출금을 상환하다'. In everyday conversation '갚다' sounds much more natural.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 선천적으로 소리를 잘 들어요.
examples.en: That child has naturally sharp hearing.
Effort is more important than innate talent.
He has a congenital heart condition.

examples.ko: 말하기 실력은 선천보다 후천적인 노력으로 늘어요.
examples.en: Speaking skill improves through acquired effort rather than what you are born with.

examples.ko: 선천과 후천 가운데 무엇이 더 중요할까요?
examples.en: Which is more important, what you are born with or what you acquire later?

examples.ko: 선천적이지 않아도 연습하면 잘할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Even if it is not innate, you can get good at it with practice.

explain: '선천'은 거의 '선천적', '선천적으로' 꼴로 써요. 반대말은 '후천'(태어난 뒤에 얻은 것)이라서 '선천적 재능, 후천적 노력'처럼 짝으로 자주 나와요. 일상에서는 '타고나다'(타고난 재능)도 많이 써요.
explain_en: '선천' is almost always used as '선천적' or '선천적으로'. Its opposite is '후천' (acquired after birth), so they often appear as a pair, like '선천적 재능, 후천적 노력'. In daily speech '타고나다' (as in '타고난 재능') is also very common.

examples.en: This cleaning agent removes grease well.

examples.ko: 얼굴 세정을 꼼꼼히 하면 피부가 깨끗해져요.
examples.en: If you cleanse your face carefully, your skin gets clear.
I'm looking for a soap with strong cleaning power.

examples.ko: 이 기계는 자동 세정 기능이 있어요.
examples.en: This machine has an automatic cleaning function.

examples.ko: 세정 후에는 물기를 완전히 말려 주세요.
examples.en: After cleaning, please dry it off completely.

examples.ko: 렌즈 세정액이 다 떨어져서 새로 샀어요.
examples.en: I ran out of lens cleaning solution, so I bought a new one.

explain: '세정'은 혼자 쓰이기보다 '세정제', '세정액', '세정력'처럼 다른 말과 붙어서 자주 나와요. 일상에서 '씻다', '닦다'라고 하는 일을 제품 설명이나 이름에서는 '세정'이라고 해요. 얼굴은 '세안'처럼 대상에 따라 따로 쓰는 말도 있어요.
explain_en: '세정' rarely stands alone; it usually joins other words, as in '세정제', '세정액' and '세정력'. What people call '씻다' or '닦다' in daily life is called '세정' in product descriptions and names. Some targets have their own word, such as '세안' for washing the face.

en: fall behind on a payment; return late (overdue)

examples.en: If you pay your card bill late, interest is added.
I am two months behind on the rent.
I returned the library book late and paid a fine.

examples.ko: 요금을 연체한 적이 한 번도 없어요.
examples.en: I have never once been late paying a bill.
Check the date so you don't fall behind on the loan payment.
I'm worried because I'm behind on my utility bills.

explain: 돈을 내야 하는 날짜를 넘기거나 빌린 책을 늦게 돌려줄 때 써요. '연체료', '연체 이자', '연체되다'와 같이 나와요. 약속에 늦는 것은 '늦다'이고, '연체하다'는 돈이나 대여물처럼 기한이 있는 것에만 써요.
explain_en: Used when you miss a payment deadline or return something borrowed, like a book, late. It appears with '연체료' (late fee), '연체 이자' (late interest) and '연체되다'. Being late for an appointment is just '늦다'; '연체하다' is only for things with a deadline, such as money or rentals.

en: long for; yearn for; desire ardently

examples.en: I long to study in Korea.
He yearned for a championship for a long time.
Many people are longing for peace.
The dream he had yearned for finally came true.
We are recruiting people who are eager for new challenges.

examples.ko: 무언가를 열망할 때 사람은 더 노력해요.
examples.en: When people long for something, they try harder.

explain: '원하다'나 '바라다'보다 훨씬 강하고 간절한 말이에요. 말로 '정말 하고 싶어요'라고 할 일을 글, 연설, 자기소개서에서는 '열망하다'로 써요. 명사 '열망'을 써서 '열망이 크다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is much stronger and more earnest than '원하다' or '바라다'. Where people would say '정말 하고 싶어요' in speech, writing, speeches and self-introductions use '열망하다'. The noun form works too, as in '열망이 크다'.

examples.en: The government promised to abolish unnecessary regulations.

examples.ko: 노동자들의 차별 철폐 요구가 점점 커지고 있어요.
examples.en: The workers' demand to eliminate discrimination keeps growing.
Abolishing a system takes a long time.

examples.ko: 관세 철폐로 가격이 내려갈 수 있어요.
examples.en: Prices could go down because tariffs are eliminated.

examples.ko: 이번 협상의 목표는 무역 장벽 철폐예요.
examples.en: The goal of this negotiation is the removal of trade barriers.

examples.ko: 많은 사람이 그 법의 철폐에 찬성했어요.
examples.en: Many people were in favor of repealing that law.

explain: '규제 철폐', '제도 철폐', '차별 철폐'처럼 오랫동안 있던 제도, 규칙, 차별을 없앨 때 써요. 일상의 물건이나 일에는 쓰지 않고 뉴스나 정치, 사회 이야기에서 나와요. 비슷한 '폐지'는 법, 제도, 시설을 없앨 때 두루 써요.
explain_en: Used for getting rid of long-standing systems, rules or discrimination, as in '규제 철폐', '제도 철폐' and '차별 철폐'. It is not used for everyday objects or tasks, only in news, politics and social topics. The similar '폐지' is used broadly for ending laws, systems and facilities.

examples.en: The old regulation was finally abolished.
If tariffs are eliminated, imported goods will get cheaper.

examples.ko: 그 제도는 몇 년 전에 철폐되었어요.
examples.en: That system was abolished a few years ago.
I want to build a society where discrimination has been eliminated.
I hope the unnecessary procedures will be done away with.

examples.ko: 장벽이 철폐되지 않으면 교류가 늘기 어려워요.
examples.en: Unless the barriers are removed, it is hard for exchange to grow.

explain: '철폐하다'는 없애는 쪽이 주어이고, '철폐되다'는 규제나 제도가 주어예요. 뉴스에서 '규제가 철폐되다'처럼 결과를 말할 때 자주 써요.
explain_en: '철폐하다' has the one doing the abolishing as its subject, while '철폐되다' takes the regulation or system as its subject. News often uses it to report the result, as in '규제가 철폐되다'.

examples.en: The government decided to abolish the outdated regulations.
The company did away with unnecessary rules.
The school plans to eliminate the complicated procedures.

examples.ko: 두 나라는 관세를 철폐하는 데 합의했어요.
examples.en: The two countries agreed to eliminate tariffs.
The voices calling for an end to discrimination grew louder.

examples.ko: 옛 제도를 철폐하고 새 방식을 도입했어요.
examples.en: They abolished the old system and introduced a new method.

explain: '규제를 철폐하다', '차별을 철폐하다'처럼 목적어가 제도, 규제, 장벽, 차별이에요. 사람이 쓰는 물건이나 일상의 일에는 쓰지 않아요. 일상에서 비슷한 상황은 '없애다'라고 해요.
explain_en: The object is a system, regulation, barrier or discrimination, as in '규제를 철폐하다' or '차별을 철폐하다'. It is not used for ordinary objects or daily matters, where people just say '없애다'.

examples.en: The government decided to send troops overseas.
The deployment period was set at six months.
There were also many opinions against sending troops.

examples.ko: 이번 파병은 평화 유지를 위한 것이에요.
examples.en: This deployment is for peacekeeping.
The families of the deployed soldiers watched the news.
The National Assembly discussed the motion to approve the deployment.

explain: '파병'은 군대를 다른 나라나 먼 곳으로 보내는 일에 써요. 비슷한 '파견'은 직원이나 전문가를 일을 맡겨 보낼 때도 쓰지만, '파병'은 군인에게만 써요. 뉴스에서 '해외 파병', '파병 동의안'처럼 자주 나와요.
explain_en: '파병' is for sending military forces to another country or a distant place. The similar '파견' can also be used for dispatching staff or experts on assignment, but '파병' is only for soldiers. News often uses it in phrases like '해외 파병' and '파병 동의안'.

examples.ko: 한국은 평화 유지를 위해 군대를 파병했어요.
examples.en: Korea sent troops for peacekeeping.
The government decided to send forces abroad.

examples.ko: 그 나라는 분쟁 지역에 평화유지군을 파병할 거예요.
examples.en: That country will send peacekeeping forces to the conflict zone.

examples.ko: 다른 나라에 군대를 파병하는 일은 신중해야 해요.
examples.en: Sending troops to another country has to be done carefully.
The unit that was sent out returned safely.
Some proposed sending troops.

explain: '군대를 파병하다', '병력을 파병하다'처럼 목적어가 군대나 부대예요. 직원이나 전문가를 보낼 때는 '파견하다'를 써요. 뉴스와 정치 이야기에서 주로 나오고 일상 대화에서는 거의 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: The object is troops or a unit, as in '군대를 파병하다' and '병력을 파병하다'. For sending staff or experts, use '파견하다'. It appears mostly in news and politics and is rarely used in everyday conversation.

en: feel empty; hollow and let down

examples.en: I feel empty because the exam I prepared so hard for was canceled.
Feeling hollow, I just looked at the sky for a long time.
The match ended so easily that it was anticlimactic.
All the effort vanished into nothing.

examples.ko: 일이 끝나고 나니 허무하다는 생각이 들었어요.
examples.en: After the work was over, I felt a sense of emptiness.
I set small goals so I wouldn't feel empty.

explain: 열심히 했는데 결과가 없거나, 기대한 것이 갑자기 사라졌을 때의 힘 빠진 마음이에요. 비슷한 '허탈하다'는 몸에 힘이 쭉 빠지는 느낌이고, '허무하다'는 모든 것이 의미 없어진 것 같은 느낌이 더 커요. '허무하게 끝나다', '허무하게 지다'처럼 부사형으로도 많이 써요.
explain_en: It describes the deflated feeling when hard work leads to nothing or something you expected suddenly disappears. The similar '허탈하다' is more about strength draining out of you, while '허무하다' leans toward a feeling that everything has become meaningless. The adverb form is common too, as in '허무하게 끝나다' and '허무하게 지다'.

examples.en: There are many short shrubs in the garden.

examples.ko: 관목은 줄기가 여러 개로 갈라져 자라요.
examples.en: Shrubs grow with their stems splitting into several branches.
We planted shrubs along the road to make a hedge.
A shrub forest continues along the middle of the mountain.

examples.ko: 이 관목에는 봄에 작은 꽃이 피어요.
examples.en: Small flowers bloom on this shrub in spring.

examples.ko: 겨울에도 관목의 잎이 푸르게 남아 있어요.
examples.en: The shrub's leaves stay green even in winter.

explain: '관목'은 키가 작고 줄기가 여러 갈래로 자라는 나무예요. 반대말은 키가 큰 '교목'이에요. 일상에서는 그냥 '나무'나 '덤불'이라고 하고, '관목'은 식물 설명이나 과학 글에서 나와요.
explain_en: '관목' is a short plant whose stems grow in several branches. Its opposite is the tall tree '교목'. In daily speech people just say '나무' or '덤불', while '관목' appears in plant descriptions and science writing.

examples.en: Beating a person is a crime.
If you beat someone, you are punished under the law.

examples.ko: 학교에서 학생을 구타하는 일은 법으로 금지돼 있어요.
examples.en: Beating students at school is banned by law.
Don't hit people; solve it with words.

examples.ko: 구타하는 장면이 나오는 영화는 아이가 보면 안 돼요.
examples.en: Children should not watch movies with scenes of beating.

examples.ko: 아이를 구타하면 안 된다는 법이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a law that says you must not beat a child.

explain: 일상에서는 '때리다'를 쓰고, '구타하다'는 뉴스, 법, 사건 이야기에서 나와요. 한 번 때리는 것보다 여러 번 심하게 때리는 느낌이 있어요. '구타', '폭행'과 같이 알아 두세요.
explain_en: Daily speech uses '때리다', while '구타하다' appears in news, law and reports of incidents. It feels more like hitting hard and repeatedly than a single blow. Learn it together with the nouns '구타' and '폭행'.

en: resident of a province (such as Gyeonggi-do or Jeju-do)

examples.ko: 도민들이 새 공항 건설에 대해 의견을 냈어요.
examples.en: The province's residents gave their opinions on building the new airport.
Most of the province's residents were in favor of this plan.
This event is open free of charge to the province's residents.
The provincial governor said they would listen to the residents' voices.

examples.ko: 도민을 위한 문화 공간이 새로 생겼어요.
examples.en: A new cultural space for the province's residents has opened.

examples.ko: 도민 설문 조사에서 교통이 가장 큰 문제로 나왔어요.
examples.en: In the survey of residents, transportation came out as the biggest problem.

explain: 경기도, 충청북도, 제주도처럼 '도'에 사는 사람을 '도민'이라고 해요. 시에 사는 사람은 '시민', 군에 사는 사람은 '군민', 구에 사는 사람은 '구민'이에요. '제주도민'처럼 지역 이름 뒤에 붙여 쓰는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: People who live in a '도' (province), such as Gyeonggi-do, Chungcheongbuk-do or Jeju-do, are called '도민'. Those living in a '시' are '시민', in a '군' are '군민', and in a '구' are '구민'. It is often attached to a region name, as in '제주도민'.

examples.ko: 옛날이야기에는 사람을 속이는 마귀가 자주 나와요.
examples.en: Old folk tales often feature demons who trick people.

examples.ko: 아이들은 영화 속 마귀를 보고 무서워했어요.
examples.en: The children were scared of the demon in the movie.
That demon tormented the villagers.

examples.ko: 마귀 같은 사람이라고 욕하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't curse someone by calling them a devil.
The brave prince fought the demon and won.
I saw a picture of what the demon looked like in a book.

explain: '마귀'는 사람을 해치거나 나쁜 길로 이끄는 악한 존재예요. '귀신'은 죽은 사람의 영혼을 말하고, '마귀'는 처음부터 악한 존재라는 느낌이에요. 옛날이야기와 종교 이야기에서 많이 나오고, 일상 대화에서는 거의 안 써요.
explain_en: '마귀' is an evil being that harms people or leads them astray. '귀신' refers to the spirit of a dead person, while '마귀' feels evil by nature. It appears often in folk tales and religious talk and is rarely used in everyday conversation.

en: all things; everything in the world

examples.en: When spring comes, all living things wake up.
There is a saying that humans are the lords of all creation.

examples.ko: 이 시는 만물에 대한 사랑을 노래해요.
examples.en: This poem sings of love for all things.
My grandmother told me to treasure everything in the world.
When winter comes, everything rests quietly.

examples.ko: 사람은 자연 속에서 만물과 함께 살아가요.
examples.en: People live together with all things in nature.

explain: 자연과 우주에 있는 모든 것을 크게 말할 때 써요. '봄이 되면 만물이 깨어난다'처럼 글, 시, 격언 같은 말투에 어울려요. 평소 대화에서는 '모든 것'이나 '세상 모든 것'이라고 해요.
explain_en: Used to speak broadly of everything in nature and the universe. It fits a written, poetic or proverb-like tone, as in '봄이 되면 만물이 깨어난다'. In ordinary conversation people say '모든 것' or '세상 모든 것'.

en: meet again after a long separation; reunite

examples.en: I was really happy to be reunited with my family after so long.
Footage of separated family members reuniting was on the news.

examples.ko: 공항에서 친구와 상봉하는 순간 눈물이 났어요.
examples.en: The moment I met my friend again at the airport, I cried.
Separated families wait for the day they can reunite.

examples.ko: 두 사람은 십 년 뒤 서울에서 상봉하기로 약속했어요.
examples.en: The two promised to meet again in Seoul ten years later.
I want to see my son again, who went into the army.

explain: 오랫동안 헤어져 있던 사람을 다시 만날 때, 특히 감동적인 재회에 써요. 일상에서 약속을 잡고 보는 '만나다'와는 느낌이 달라요. '이산가족 상봉'이라는 말이 대표적이에요.
explain_en: Used when meeting someone again after a long separation, especially an emotional reunion. It feels different from '만나다', which covers ordinary meetings arranged in daily life. The typical phrase is '이산가족 상봉' (reunion of separated families).

examples.ko: 두 사람은 결혼식에서 서로 사랑하겠다고 서약했어요.
examples.en: At the wedding, the two pledged to love each other.
New employees pledge to keep secrets.
The sight of them raising their hands and taking the oath was impressive.

examples.ko: 회원들은 규칙을 지키기로 서약한 뒤 가입했어요.
examples.en: The members joined after pledging to follow the rules.
The president will swear to uphold the constitution.
After taking the pledge, my resolve grew stronger.

explain: '약속하다'보다 훨씬 공식적이고 무거운 말이에요. 사람들 앞이나 문서로 지키겠다고 다짐할 때 써요. 비슷한 '맹세하다'는 마음속 다짐이나 감정이 더 강하고, '서약하다'는 '서약서'를 쓰는 것처럼 공식적인 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It is much more formal and weighty than '약속하다'. It is used when committing to something before people or in writing. The similar '맹세하다' is about a heartfelt vow, while '서약하다' has an official feel, like signing a '서약서' (written pledge).

examples.ko: 그는 세속을 떠나 산에서 살기로 했어요.
examples.en: He decided to leave the worldly life and live in the mountains.
If you let go of worldly greed, your mind becomes calm.
The monk is not interested in worldly things.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 세속에 물들지 않은 순수한 사람이에요.
examples.en: That person is pure and untouched by the ways of the world.

examples.ko: 세속 사회에서는 돈과 지위가 중요하게 여겨져요.
examples.en: In secular society, money and status are considered important.
There are things more precious than worldly values.

explain: 종교나 수도 생활과 반대로, 돈과 명예를 따지는 보통 사람들의 세상을 말해요. '세속을 떠나다', '세속적인 성공'처럼 쓰고, '세속적'이라고 하면 돈이나 지위를 중요하게 여긴다는 느낌이 있어요. 글이나 종교, 철학 이야기에서 주로 나와요.
explain_en: It refers to the world of ordinary people who care about money and fame, as opposed to religious or monastic life. It is used in phrases like '세속을 떠나다' and '세속적인 성공', and '세속적' carries the sense of valuing money or status. It appears mostly in writing and in religious or philosophical talk.

en: police wanted notice; search for a suspect by the authorities

examples.en: That person is currently wanted by the police.
The police put up wanted posters for the criminal.

examples.ko: 수배가 내려진 뒤 그는 도망 다녔어요.
examples.en: After the wanted notice was issued, he went on the run.
At the airport, they check the wanted photos.
He was put on the wanted list on a fraud charge.
I asked for the wanted notice to be lifted.

explain: 경찰이 범인을 잡으려고 전국에 알리는 일이에요. '지명 수배', '수배 전단', '수배 중'처럼 쓰고, 주로 뉴스나 사건 이야기에서 나와요. 일상에서 사람이나 물건을 '찾다'라고 하는 것과는 달라요.
explain_en: It means the police spreading word nationwide to catch a suspect, as in '지명 수배', '수배 전단' and '수배 중'. It appears mainly in news and crime stories. It is different from the everyday '찾다' for looking for people or things.

en: be wanted by the police; be put on a wanted list

examples.en: He was put on the wanted list on a fraud charge.
The wanted criminal was caught yesterday.
This person is wanted across the country.
Once you are wanted, it is hard even to leave the country.

examples.ko: 오랫동안 수배되던 남자가 스스로 경찰서에 찾아갔어요.
examples.en: The man who had long been wanted went to the police station on his own.

examples.ko: 수배되지 않았다면 그는 마음 편히 살았을 거예요.
examples.en: If he had not been wanted, he would have lived with peace of mind.

explain: '수배하다'는 경찰이 쫓는 쪽이고, '수배되다'는 쫓기는 사람이 주어예요. '지명수배되다'처럼도 쓰고, 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: '수배하다' is from the side of the police doing the pursuing, while '수배되다' takes the pursued person as the subject. It is also used as '지명수배되다' and shows up often in news.

examples.en: He was called the guardian of the village.

examples.ko: 영화 속 수호자는 아이들을 지켜 줘요.
examples.en: The guardian in the movie protects the children.
This statue symbolizes the guardian of the city.
My mother is a dependable protector of our family.

examples.ko: 게임에서 마지막 문을 지키는 수호자가 나와요.
examples.en: In the game, a guardian who protects the final gate appears.

examples.ko: 마을 사람들은 수호자에게 감사 인사를 전했어요.
examples.en: The villagers expressed their thanks to the guardian.

explain: 나라, 마을, 가족, 가치 같은 것을 지키는 사람이나 존재예요. '보호자'는 아이나 환자를 돌보는 가족을 말하고, '수호자'는 공격이나 위험에서 지켜 주는 사람에게 써요. 영화, 게임, 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: A person or being who protects a country, village, family or value. '보호자' refers to a family member who looks after a child or patient, while '수호자' is for someone who guards against attack or danger. It is common in movies, games and stories.

en: talk this and that about; bring up and go on about (often critically)

examples.ko: 그는 내 실수를 운운하며 계속 화를 냈어요.
examples.en: He kept getting angry, going on about my mistake.

examples.ko: 아직 확실하지 않은데 벌써 결과를 운운하지 마세요.
examples.en: It's not certain yet, so don't talk about the results already.
My friend looked down on me, bringing up my age.

examples.ko: 월급을 운운하기 전에 맡은 일부터 하세요.
examples.en: Before you bring up your pay, do the work you were given.

examples.ko: 사람들이 뒤에서 내 성적을 운운하는 게 싫어요.
examples.en: I don't like people talking about my grades behind my back.

examples.ko: 그는 모임에서 늘 자기 학벌을 운운해요.
examples.en: At gatherings he is always bringing up his educational background.

explain: 'A를 운운하다'는 어떤 일을 이러쿵저러쿵 말하는 것인데, 말하는 사람이 못마땅하다는 느낌이 들어가요. 그래서 칭찬이나 좋은 이야기에는 잘 쓰지 않고, 불만이나 비난을 할 때 자주 나와요. 중립적으로 말하려면 '언급하다'를 써요.
explain_en: 'A를 운운하다' means to talk about something this way and that, with a tone that the speaker disapproves. It is rarely used for praise or good news and often appears in complaints or criticism. For a neutral version, use '언급하다'.

examples.ko: 이 농장은 인위를 더하지 않고 채소를 키워요.
examples.en: This farm grows vegetables without adding human interference.
The artificial taste is too strong, so I don't like it.
We ride a boat on a lake that was made by people.
This photo looks too staged, so it feels awkward.

examples.ko: 자연을 인위적으로 바꾸면 문제가 생길 수 있어요.
examples.en: Changing nature artificially can cause problems.

examples.ko: 인위적 조작 없이 자연스럽게 자란 채소예요.
examples.en: These are vegetables that grew naturally, without artificial manipulation.

explain: '인위'는 거의 '인위적', '인위적으로' 꼴로 써요. '인공'이 사람이 만든 물건(인공 눈물)에 쓰이는 반면, '인위적'은 억지로 꾸민 듯한 느낌이 있어요. 반대로 자연 그대로면 '자연스럽다'라고 해요.
explain_en: '인위' is almost always used as '인위적' or '인위적으로'. While '인공' describes something made by people (as in '인공 눈물'), '인위적' carries a feeling of being forced or staged. The opposite, when things are left as they are, is '자연스럽다'.

examples.en: Small efforts contributed to a big success.
We praised the player who helped the team win.

examples.ko: 환경 보호에 일조하고 싶어서 텀블러를 써요.
examples.en: I use a tumbler because I want to do my part for the environment.

examples.ko: 우리 가게가 지역 발전에 일조할 수 있으면 좋겠어요.
examples.en: I hope our shop can contribute to the development of the area.

examples.ko: 봉사 활동이 사회 분위기를 바꾸는 데 일조해요.
examples.en: Volunteer work helps change the mood of society.

examples.ko: 자원봉사자들이 행사 성공에 일조하는 모습이 보기 좋았어요.
examples.en: It was nice to see the volunteers helping make the event a success.

explain: '~에 일조하다'꼴로 써요. 큰 일의 일부를 맡아서 도움이 된다는 말이에요. 일상에서는 '도움이 되다', '한몫하다'라고 하고, '일조하다'는 격식 있는 글이나 연설에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is used in the pattern '~에 일조하다', for helping a larger effort by playing a part in it. In daily speech people say '도움이 되다' or '한몫하다', while '일조하다' is common in formal writing and speeches.

examples.en: That mayor succeeded in being reelected.

examples.ko: 대통령 재선을 위한 선거 운동이 시작됐어요.
examples.en: The campaign for the president's reelection has begun.
The news said that reelection looks certain.
He is a second-term lawmaker, so he has a lot of experience.
The citizens were surprised by the news of the bid for reelection.
People say reelection will be hard this time too.

explain: 같은 자리(대통령, 시장, 의원)에 다시 뽑히는 일이에요. 처음 뽑힌 것은 '초선', 두 번째는 '재선', 세 번째는 '3선'이라고 해요. 선거 뉴스에서 자주 나오고 '재선 의원'처럼 횟수를 말할 때도 써요.
explain_en: It means being elected again to the same post (president, mayor, lawmaker). The first election is '초선', the second '재선', the third '3선'. It appears often in election news and is also used to count terms, as in '재선 의원'.

examples.en: He was reelected as mayor.
The reelected president gave a first speech.
It is not easy for a sitting mayor to be reelected.
If reelected, you can work four more years.
They say he is likely to be reelected.
He was not reelected in this election.

explain: '재선되다'는 선거에서 다시 뽑히는 쪽이 주어예요. '시장으로 재선되다', '의원에 재선되다'처럼 자리를 같이 써요. 처음 뽑힐 때는 '당선되다'를 써요.
explain_en: The subject of '재선되다' is the person who is elected again. The post is stated with it, as in '시장으로 재선되다' and '의원에 재선되다'. For being elected the first time, use '당선되다'.
